content.question: Is the rubber coolant hose __________ enough to bend safely when the engine vibrates while it is in use? (can bend easily without breaking)
After proper lubrication, the bearing surfaces were __________, allowing the shaft to rotate without friction. (has no rough or uneven parts)
Were the guide rods __________ after the alignment check was completed in the workshop? (not bent or curved)
The mounting bolts are __________, and the machine does not shift while it is running. (fixed strongly and securely)
The cutting tool was too __________, which made it difficult to machine the steel workpiece smoothly. (solid and difficult to press or cut)
The cast metal surface is __________, so it needs grinding before final assembly. (not smooth; uneven to touch)
The belt connections were __________, so the instructor stopped the machine for safety reasons. (not fixed firmly; can move easily)
The gears were __________ after long use, and they were replaced during maintenance. (damaged or weakened by long use)

activity_b.text: Good morning.
Today, we are going to talk about the properties of different materials and how they are used in technical work.
Let me begin with this twelve-millimetre-thick steel bar.
This processed structural steel is very rigid and firm, and I am pressing it with my hands.
I am trying to bend it, but it is not bending at all.
Is it flexible?
No, it is not, but it remains stable under load, even during continuous use.
In construction and mechanical work, parts like this are not decorative; they are load-bearing and structural.
As most of you are aware, last semester, six-millimetre bars were used for benches in front of the school.
However, they were not durable or stable enough, and they bent under heavy weight over time.
Now, take a look at this sixty-five-millimetre plastic pipe.
It is lightweight, flexible, and smooth.
I am bending it slightly, and it changes shape easily.
Is it rigid?
No, it is not.
Is it strong?
Yes, it is strong enough for insulation purposes, but it is not designed to carry weight.
It is not heat-resistant, so it is unsuitable near engines or heating units.
This four-millimetre-thick glass panel, here on the left, is smooth, transparent, and brittle.
I am touching the surface now, and it feels smooth and cold.
Is it safe under impact?
No, it is not.
Because of that, it is used only for viewing panels and protective covers, not for safety barriers.
Here, I have a fifteen-centimetre rubber gasket.
It is flexible, durable, and elastic, so it is used to seal joints and prevent leaks.
I am stretching it slightly to demonstrate its elasticity.
However, if the surface is contaminated with dust or oil, the seal is not effective, and leakage may occur.
Finally, this food-grade stainless steel surface is smooth, hygienic, non-porous, and easy to clean.
I am wiping it with a cloth now.
Is it porous?
No, it is not.
Because it is hygienic and corrosion-resistant, it is widely used in food-processing and training environments.
So remember, a material is not good or bad by itself.
It is suitable or unsuitable depending on its properties, condition, and application.
